newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares fall sharply in kerb dealing.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares fall sharply in kerb dealing.

text.p: The Congress party's decision to withdraw support to the ruling coalition government provoked panic selling in kerb trade on Sunday, brokers said.

"Panic has set in due to the fears that the coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda might collapse following withdrawal of support by the Congress party," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Associates.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority United Front alliance controls some 178 deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha, or lower house. The Congress has 142 deputies.
Shares of country's largest private firm, Reliance Industries, dropped 16.75 rupees, or 5.8 percent, to 270.00, brokers said.
State Bank of India lost 18.10 rupees to 285.00.
It was not immediately clear if Congress's decision meant the 10-month-old government led by Deve Gowda would have to resign and call a snap mid-term poll.
Congress officials said the withdrawal decision followed "attempts by the United Front" to split the Congress party in the key northern state of Uttar Pradesh.

In the budget for 1997/98 (April-March), Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced sweeping cuts in corporate and personal taxes. Parliament had been expected to vote on the proposed budget after reconvening in the second half of April.
